title: London man who died after arrest remembered as sports-loving free spirit
subtitle: Fabian Hart, 34, of London, died on Tuesday after being arrested a day earlier
article: Eleven-year-old Fabian Hart didn't hesitate to barrel down a giant water slide, leaving his older brothers and step-dad in his wake.
"Boom, he was down and gone. You couldn't keep that kid from anything," said Hart's mom, Stephanie Gajewski. "He was a real daredevil, a real free spirit."
Hart, 34, died on Tuesday after being arrested a day earlier by London police, picked up for breaching the conditions of his bail.
The province's police watchdog, the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), is investigating his death.
"Fabian loved to play sports, he loved playing hockey and soccer and he played baseball for a while," said his mother.
With his three brothers, Hart loved to play in the backyard and roughhouse.
"They were typical boys and they did typical boy things," Gajewski said. "He loved to skateboard, they built ramps."
When he was a bit older, he spent some time in New Zealand, where his mom is from.
Hart struggled with an addiction to alcohol.

Born in London, he lived in West Lorne for about five years before his parents separated and he went to live with his mom and three brothers to St. Thomas. The family also lived in Montreal and Winnipeg, but Hart moved in with his dad when he was 14 years old.
The family is devastated by the news but knew that Hart struggled, Gajewski said.
"It hurts. He was a lost soul," she said.
A family friend said Hart was a skilled electrician, despite not having any formal education in the trade.
Hart was arrested at around 3:30 p.m. on Feb. 1. He was taken to London police headquarters, processed, and put in a cell.
At about 9 a.m. the next day, Hart told officers he wasn't feeling well. An ambulance took him to hospital, where he died.
The SIU investigates when there is a serious injury or death to a person who comes into contact with police.
An autopsy was done Wednesday, but family members don't yet know the results.
One subject officer, four witness officers, and two witnesses have been identified by the SIU.
